Resolving Engine B's underperformance requires a unified three-part architectural overhaul across the cluster's signal, exit, and execution layers. ## **Track 3: Exchange-Native Trigger Orders and Dual-Layer Execution on Hyperliquid L1**

### **HyperCore Trigger Order Microstructure, Mark-Price Basis, and Slippage Collars**

Implementing stop-loss and take-profit architectures on Hyperliquid L1 (HyperCore, running on HyperBFT consensus with ![][image387] block times and sub-second single-slot finality) requires accounting for three protocol-level mechanics that differ sharply from centralized exchanges6.  
First, all native conditional orders on HyperCore (t: {"trigger": {"isMarket": bool, "triggerPx": string, "tpsl": "tp" | "sl"}}) evaluate their activation condition against the Mark Price—a manipulation-resistant blend of external CEX oracle feeds and local HyperCore median bid, ask, and last-trade inputs—rather than the last traded price or top-of-book mid4. While this protects positions from premature stop-outs caused by isolated thin-book wicks on the last-trade feed9, it introduces mark-to-book basis lag during rapid order-book sweeps. When an aggressive liquidation cascade originates on Hyperliquid's L2 book, the local best bid or ask can sweep ![][image388] through a stop level before the blended Mark Price crosses triggerPx9. Conversely, if an external oracle spikes while Hyperliquid's local book lags, the Mark Price can trigger the stop order even when no local trade has printed at triggerPx9.  
Second, Hyperliquid does not implement unbounded market orders5. Every order submitted to /exchange—including a trigger order with isMarket: true—requires a valid limit price string p (limit\_px)5. When triggerPx is breached by the Mark Price, HyperCore converts an isMarket: true trigger into an immediate-or-cancel (Ioc) aggressive limit order using p as the worst-acceptable fill price5. If an execution client sets p equal to triggerPx (or within a few ticks of triggerPx), any block-level price gap across triggerPx causes the triggered order to fail to cross resting liquidity beyond p, resulting in an iocCancelRejected status or an unfilled order while the position plummets past the stop6. Consequently, for any exchange-native disaster stop-loss (tpsl: "sl", isMarket: true, reduceOnly: true), p must be configured with a ![][image389] protective slippage collar beyond triggerPx (p \= format\_px(trigger\_px \* 0.95) for a long position's sell stop, and p \= format\_px(trigger\_px \* 1.05) for a short position's buy stop) to guarantee execution certainty across flash gaps6.  
Third, Take-Profit orders must always rest directly on the CLOB (t: {"limit": {"tif": "Gtc"}}, r: true) rather than use native tpsl: "tp" trigger orders4. If a take-profit is submitted as a native trigger order (tpsl: "tp"), the order sits off-book in the conditional trigger pool (waitingForTrigger) until Mark Price reaches triggerPx, at which point isMarket: true fires as an aggressive Taker order—forfeiting the ![][image1] Maker rebate and paying ![][image15] Taker fee plus crossing slippage6. Even if isMarket: false is specified on a trigger TP, the limit order is only injected into the CLOB after Mark Price touches triggerPx, placing it at the very back of the time-priority queue6.

### **IP-Weight vs. Address-Volume Rate Limits: The Case Against Continuous Exchange Ratcheting**

A central architectural trade-off in Track 3 is whether Engine B should maintain its Chandelier trailing stop entirely on the exchange—by sending /exchange modify actions (type: "modify") to ratchet triggerPx on every favorable price increment—or monitor the dynamic Chandelier ratchet client-side in the 1.5-second L2 WebSocket daemon (Fast-Sentinel) while keeping a wide catastrophe backup trigger on HyperCore13. While continuous exchange-side modification appears attractive from a naive fault-tolerance perspective, it is mathematically fatal for a ![][image390] account on Hyperliquid due to the protocol's two-tiered rate-limiting architecture2.  
At the first tier, all REST calls across /info and /exchange share an aggregate per-IP weight quota of ![][image391] (![][image392])2. Every /exchange action (order, modify, batchModify, cancel, cancelByCloid) costs ![][image393] for unbatched or small-batch calls8. Provided the Rust cluster streams l2Book, allMids, candle, and orderUpdates via WebSockets (which allow up to 10 connections, 1,000 subscriptions, and 2,000 outbound messages/min per IP) rather than polling /info via REST2, the ![][image394] IP limit is never threatened by order modifications.  
At the second tier, however, Hyperliquid enforces a strict per-address action quota scaled by cumulative traded volume to prevent order-book spam from small accounts8. Every wallet address starts with an initial buffer of ![][image395], and thereafter earns exactly ![][image396] of cumulative filled notional traded since address inception8:  
![][image397]  
Crucially, while a batched request of ![][image398] orders or modifies counts as ![][image399] toward the IP limit, it counts as ![][image398] full requests toward the address-based limit8. Furthermore, if expiresAfter is used and an order expires due to staleness, it penalizes the address quota by ![][image400]4. Once ![][image401], the address enters hard rate-limit throttling, restricting the entire account to ![][image402] (![][image403] or ![][image404])8.  
The table below quantifies the exact address-based request budget for a ![][image405] notional position (![][image406] round-trip volume ![][image407], or ![][image408]) and traces the trajectory of the ![][image409]\-request startup buffer over ![][image410]4:

| Rate-Limit Metric / Architectural Regime | Engine A Baseline (1m OU Alo Loop) | Engine B: Continuous 1.5s Exchange modify Ratchet | Engine B: Dual-Layer Fast-Sentinel \+ Disaster SL | Microstructural & Quota Impact on Cluster |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Round-Trip Traded Volume (![][image411])** | **![][image412]** | **![][image412]** | **![][image412]** | Generates ![][image413] of address quota per trade (![][image414] per A+B pair)8. |
| **API Requests Consumed per Trade** | **![][image415]** (Alo entry/reprice \+ TP \+ ratchet) | ![][image416] (continuous modify \+ Alo retries) | ![][image417] (batched TP+SL \+ 1 BE modify \+ cleanup) | High-frequency Alo rejections (badAloPxRejected) and stop modifies each cost 1 full address request8. |
| **Combined Cluster Quota Balance (per A+B Pair)** | — | ![][image418] **(Net Deficit)** | **![][image419] (Net Surplus)** | Continuous exchange ratcheting consumes ![][image420] vs. ![][image414] earned; Dual-Layer consumes ![][image421]8. |
| **10,000-Request Startup Buffer at 222 Trade Pairs** | — | ![][image422] **(Buffer Exhausted)** | **![][image423]** | Continuous ratcheting bankrupts the ![][image409] initial buffer at trade pair ![][image424]8. |
| **10,000-Request Startup Buffer at 300 Trade Pairs** | — | **Throttled (![][image425])** | **![][image426]** | Once throttled to ![][image403], neither Engine A nor Engine B can manage live orders8. |

### **Dual-Layer Stop Architecture Comparison and Lifecycle**

To achieve institutional fault tolerance while maintaining the ![][image427] address-quota surplus per trade pair, Engine B must partition stop management into a client-side primary layer (Fast-Sentinel) and an exchange-native catastrophe layer (HyperCore Disaster Trigger)6:

| Architectural Dimension | Layer 1: Client-Side Fast-Sentinel Soft Stop / Ratchet | Layer 2: Exchange-Native HyperCore Disaster Trigger Stop |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Primary Role** | Executes normal initial stops (![][image377]), progressive giveback ratchets (![][image378] progress / ![][image26] giveback), and L2 OBI collapse exits. | Protects against Rust daemon panic, host/VPS crash, local WebSocket disconnect, or catastrophic flash-crash gap across the soft stop. |
| **Trigger Price Reference** | L2 WebSocket Micro-Price & Book Imbalance (1.5s loop, zero mark-oracle lag)2. | HyperCore blended **Mark Price** (triggerPx) evaluated on-chain every \~400ms block6. |
| **Initial Stop Placement** | Monitored locally in Rust memory at ![][image428]. | Submitted to /exchange at entry fill at ![][image429] (![][image430] buffer behind Layer 1 so Mark-Price basis noise never front-runs Fast-Sentinel). |
| **Ratchet Update Policy** | Updated continuously in local memory every 1.5 seconds (0 API weight, 0 address quota). | Modified via /exchange (type: "modify") **at most ONCE per trade**: when intrabar MFE reaches ![][image431], triggerPx is ratcheted to breakeven (![][image432])13. |
| **Order Type & Slippage Collar** | Aggressive Limit Ioc with a tight ![][image433] (![][image17]) slippage collar, or 500ms Alo book-top attempt if spread is wide2. | Native Trigger (tpsl: "sl", isMarket: true, r: true) with a wide ![][image389] **(![][image434]) worst-price limit collar p** to guarantee fill across flash gaps6. |
| **API Quota Cost per Trade** | **![][image435]** during monitoring; ![][image399] (Ioc order) \+ ![][image399] (batch cancel of resting TP & Disaster SL) if triggered8. | ![][image399] at entry (batched with resting Maker TP \= 1 IP weight, 2 address requests) \+ at most ![][image436] at breakeven activation8. |

Furthermore, while Hyperliquid provides a native Dead Man's Switch (scheduleCancel) that cancels all open orders if no heartbeat is received within a specified timeout (minimum 5-second delay, maximum 10 triggers per UTC day, reset at 00:00 UTC)12, it must be used with strict state discipline. Because scheduleCancel cancels all open orders on the account—including resting reduce-only Trigger Stop-Loss and Maker Take-Profit orders—leaving scheduleCancel armed after an entry has filled would strip the position of its exchange-native Disaster Stop during a prolonged VPS outage16. Consequently, scheduleCancel should only be armed while non-reduce-only entry orders are resting, and explicitly disarmed ("time": null) once the entry fills and the reduce-only exit bracket is confirmed resting on HyperCore16.

### **Production Rust SDK and Wire-Level Payload Specifications**

To eliminate silent order rejections (tickRejected, minTradeNtlRejected, badTriggerPxRejected, oracleRejected)6, the Rust execution layer must enforce four HyperCore wire-format invariants before EIP-712 Phantom Agent signing (Chain ID 1337\)6. First, every price string (p and triggerPx) for perpetuals must have at most 5 significant figures and at most ![][image437] decimal places, with trailing zeros stripped (round\_wire\_px)2. Second, every size string (s) must be truncated strictly downward (floor\_hyperliquid\_sz) to szDecimals decimal places as defined in /info meta.universe for asset index a2. Third, each leg must be assigned a deterministic 128-bit hexadecimal Client Order ID (cloid, formatted as 0x \+ 32 hex characters) prior to network transmission so that the order can be modified (type: "modify") or canceled (type: "cancelByCloid") even if an HTTP response is delayed2. Fourth, when canceling trigger orders via cancel or cancelByCloid, the fast-cancel flag "f": true must never be set (as HyperCore rejects "f": true on trigger orders, and rejects actions hashed with "f": false), requiring f to be omitted entirely16.

\#\[derive(Debug, Clone)\]  
pub struct PreBreakoutTelemetry {  
    pub donchian\_high\_20\_prev: f64,  
    pub donchian\_low\_20\_prev: f64,  
    pub atr\_20\_prev: f64,  
    pub tr\_5\_mean\_prev: f64,  
    pub close\_std\_20\_prev: f64,  
    pub sqz\_persistence\_5\_prev: usize,  
    pub current\_px: f64,  
    pub close\_60m\_ago: f64,  
    pub z\_60: f64,  
    pub active\_swing\_extreme\_60m: f64,  
    pub hmm\_p\_trend: f64,  
}

\#\[derive(Debug, Clone)\]  
pub struct SqueezeGateVerdict {  
    pub approved: bool,  
    pub ndw\_20: f64,  
    pub sr\_20: f64,  
    pub rmb\_atr: f64,  
    pub overshoot\_atr: f64,  
}

/// Evaluates causal Track 1 Volatility-Squeeze and Residual Move Budget conditions  
pub fn evaluate\_pre\_breakout\_gate(  
    cfg: \&AssetBreakoutConfig,  
    t: \&PreBreakoutTelemetry,  
    is\_long: bool,  
) \-\> SqueezeGateVerdict {  
    let atr \= t.atr\_20\_prev.max(1e-9);  
    let ndw\_20 \= (t.donchian\_high\_20\_prev \- t.donchian\_low\_20\_prev) / atr;  
    let sr\_20 \= (4.0 \* t.close\_std\_20\_prev) / (3.0 \* atr);  
    let vr\_5\_20 \= t.tr\_5\_mean\_prev / atr;

    let d\_60\_atr \= (t.current\_px \- t.close\_60m\_ago).abs() / atr;  
    let e\_imp\_atr \= if is\_long {  
        (t.current\_px \- t.active\_swing\_extreme\_60m).max(0.0) / atr  
    } else {  
        (t.active\_swing\_extreme\_60m \- t.current\_px).max(0.0) / atr  
    };

    let overshoot\_atr \= if is\_long {  
        (t.current\_px \- t.donchian\_high\_20\_prev).max(0.0) / atr  
    } else {  
        (t.donchian\_low\_20\_prev \- t.current\_px).max(0.0) / atr  
    };

    let consumed\_budget \= (0.5 \* ndw\_20).max(e\_imp\_atr) \+ 0.50 \* overshoot\_atr;  
    let rmb\_atr \= cfg.b\_max\_atr \- consumed\_budget;

    let is\_coiled \= ndw\_20 \>= cfg.min\_ndw\_20  
        && ndw\_20 \<= cfg.max\_ndw\_20  
        && sr\_20 \<= cfg.max\_sr\_20  
        && t.sqz\_persistence\_5\_prev \>= 3  
        && vr\_5\_20 \<= cfg.max\_vr\_5\_20;

    let exhaustion\_clear \= t.z\_60.abs() \<= cfg.max\_z60  
        && d\_60\_atr \<= cfg.max\_d60\_atr  
        && overshoot\_atr \<= cfg.max\_overshoot\_atr  
        && rmb\_atr \>= cfg.min\_rmb\_atr;

    // When coiled compression is verified, HMM dwell lag is bypassed (0-bar dwell, P\_Trend \>= 0.62)  
    let hmm\_clear \= t.hmm\_p\_trend \>= 0.62;

    SqueezeGateVerdict {  
        approved: is\_coiled && exhaustion\_clear && hmm\_clear,  
        ndw\_20,  
        sr\_20,  
        rmb\_atr,  
        overshoot\_atr,  
    }  
}

/// Rounds perpetual price to \<= 5 significant figures and \<= (6 \- sz\_decimals) decimals  
pub fn round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(px: f64, sz\_decimals: u32) \-\> f64 {  
    if px \<= 0.0 {  
        return 0.0;  
    }  
    let max\_dec \= 6u32.saturating\_sub(sz\_decimals) as i32;  
    let digits \= px.log10().floor() as i32 \+ 1;  
    let sig\_dec \= (5 \- digits).max(0);  
    let decimals \= max\_dec.min(sig\_dec);  
    let factor \= 10f64.powi(decimals);  
    (px \* factor).round() / factor  
}

/// Rounds base asset size strictly DOWN to sz\_decimals to prevent margin/balance rejection  
pub fn floor\_hyperliquid\_sz(sz: f64, sz\_decimals: u32) \-\> f64 {  
    let factor \= 10f64.powi(sz\_decimals as i32);  
    (sz \* factor).floor() / factor  
}

/// Places unitary resting Reduce-Only Maker TP \+ Exchange-Native Disaster Stop-Market  
pub async fn place\_hybrid\_exit\_bracket(  
    exchange: \&ExchangeClient,  
    wallet: \&LocalWallet,  
    cfg: \&AssetBreakoutConfig,  
    is\_long\_position: bool,  
    entry\_px: f64,  
    position\_sz: f64,  
    atr\_20: f64,  
) \-\> Result\<(Uuid, Uuid, Option\<u64\>), String\> {  
    let clean\_sz \= floor\_hyperliquid\_sz(position\_sz, cfg.sz\_decimals);  
    if clean\_sz \* entry\_px \< 11.0 {  
        return Err("Position notional below \$11.00 safe floor".to\_string());  
    }

    let exit\_is\_buy \= \!is\_long\_position;  
    let raw\_tp\_px \= if is\_long\_position {  
        entry\_px \+ cfg.k\_tp\_atr \* atr\_20  
    } else {  
        entry\_px \- cfg.k\_tp\_atr \* atr\_20  
    };  
    let tp\_px \= round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(raw\_tp\_px, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    let raw\_sl\_trig\_px \= if is\_long\_position {  
        entry\_px \- cfg.k\_disaster\_sl\_atr \* atr\_20  
    } else {  
        entry\_px \+ cfg.k\_disaster\_sl\_atr \* atr\_20  
    };  
    let sl\_trigger\_px \= round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(raw\_sl\_trig\_px, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    // 5.0% protective slippage collar on worst-acceptable limit\_px for triggered Stop-Market  
    let raw\_sl\_limit\_px \= if is\_long\_position {  
        sl\_trigger\_px \* 0.95  
    } else {  
        sl\_trigger\_px \* 1.05  
    };  
    let sl\_limit\_px \= round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(raw\_sl\_limit\_px, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    let cloid\_tp \= Uuid::new\_v4();  
    let cloid\_sl \= Uuid::new\_v4();

    // Leg 1: Resting Reduce-Only Maker Limit Take-Profit on L1 CLOB  
    let maker\_tp\_order \= ClientOrderRequest {  
        asset: cfg.symbol.to\_string(),  
        is\_buy: exit\_is\_buy,  
        reduce\_only: true,  
        limit\_px: tp\_px,  
        sz: clean\_sz,  
        cloid: Some(cloid\_tp),  
        order\_type: ClientOrder::Limit(ClientLimit {  
            tif: "Gtc".to\_string(),  
        }),  
    };

    // Leg 2: Exchange-Native Disaster Stop-Market Trigger Order  
    let disaster\_sl\_order \= ClientOrderRequest {  
        asset: cfg.symbol.to\_string(),  
        is\_buy: exit\_is\_buy,  
        reduce\_only: true,  
        limit\_px: sl\_limit\_px,  
        sz: clean\_sz,  
        cloid: Some(cloid\_sl),  
        order\_type: ClientOrder::Trigger(ClientTrigger {  
            is\_market: true,  
            trigger\_px: sl\_trigger\_px,  
            tpsl: "sl".to\_string(),  
        }),  
    };

    let response \= exchange  
        .bulk\_order(vec\!\[maker\_tp\_order, disaster\_sl\_order\], Some(wallet))  
        .await  
        .map\_err(|e| format\!("HyperCore bulk\_order error: {e}"))?;

    let mut sl\_oid: Option\<u64\> \= None;  
    if let ExchangeResponseStatus::Ok(resp\_data) \= response {  
        if let Some(data) \= resp\_data.data {  
            if let Some(ExchangeDataStatus::Resting(resting)) \= data.statuses.get(1) {  
                sl\_oid \= Some(resting.oid);  
            }  
        }  
    }

    Ok((cloid\_tp, cloid\_sl, sl\_oid))  
}

/// One-time milestone ratchet of Exchange-Native Disaster Stop to Breakeven (+0.05x ATR)  
pub async fn ratchet\_disaster\_stop\_to\_breakeven(  
    exchange: \&ExchangeClient,  
    wallet: \&LocalWallet,  
    cfg: \&AssetBreakoutConfig,  
    sl\_oid: u64,  
    is\_long\_position: bool,  
    entry\_px: f64,  
    position\_sz: f64,  
    atr\_20: f64,  
) \-\> Result\<(), String\> {  
    let exit\_is\_buy \= \!is\_long\_position;  
    let clean\_sz \= floor\_hyperliquid\_sz(position\_sz, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    let raw\_be\_trig \= if is\_long\_position {  
        entry\_px \+ 0.05 \* atr\_20  
    } else {  
        entry\_px \- 0.05 \* atr\_20  
    };  
    let be\_trigger\_px \= round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(raw\_be\_trig, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    let raw\_be\_limit \= if is\_long\_position {  
        be\_trigger\_px \* 0.95  
    } else {  
        be\_trigger\_px \* 1.05  
    };  
    let be\_limit\_px \= round\_hyperliquid\_perp\_px(raw\_be\_limit, cfg.sz\_decimals);

    let modify\_req \= ClientModifyRequest {  
        oid: sl\_oid,  
        order: ClientOrderRequest {  
            asset: cfg.symbol.to\_string(),  
            is\_buy: exit\_is\_buy,  
            reduce\_only: true,  
            limit\_px: be\_limit\_px,  
            sz: clean\_sz,  
            cloid: Some(Uuid::new\_v4()),  
            order\_type: ClientOrder::Trigger(ClientTrigger {  
                is\_market: true,  
                trigger\_px: be\_trigger\_px,  
                tpsl: "sl".to\_string(),  
            }),  
        },  
    };

    exchange  
        .modify(modify\_req, Some(wallet))  
        .await  
        .map\_err(|e| format\!("HyperCore modify disaster SL failed: {e}"))?;

    Ok(())  
}

/// Cancels remaining sibling leg by cloid upon position closure (omits 'f: true' for trigger compatibility)  
pub async fn cancel\_sibling\_by\_cloid(  
    exchange: \&ExchangeClient,  
    wallet: \&LocalWallet,  
    cfg: \&AssetBreakoutConfig,  
    cloid: Uuid,  
) \-\> Result\<(), String\> {  
    let cancel\_req \= ClientCancelRequestCloid {  
        asset: cfg.symbol.to\_string(),  
        cloid,  
    };  
    exchange  
        .cancel\_by\_cloid(cancel\_req, Some(wallet))  
        .await  
        .map\_err(|e| format\!("HyperCore cancel\_by\_cloid failed: {e}"))?;  
    Ok(())  
}

## **Production Deployment Roadmap for the Dual-Engine Cluster**

Transitioning Engine B from negative-EV late chasing to positive-EV coiled breakout harvesting without disrupting Engine A's live 1-minute mean-reversion loop proceeds across three deterministic phases. In the first phase, the trailing 60-minute 1-minute return series from Engine A's ring buffer is exposed directly to Engine B so that ![][image76], ![][image77], ![][image21], ![][image22], and ![][image23] are computed in ![][image444] time on every 1.5-second L2 tick, bypassing the 1-to-2 bar 15-minute HMM dwell delay whenever evaluate\_pre\_breakout\_gate returns approved \== true. In the second phase, the open-ended Wilder ![][image13] Chandelier exit is replaced with place\_hybrid\_exit\_bracket, setting resting Reduce-Only Maker Limit TPs at ![][image445] (BTC), ![][image104] (ETH), ![][image446] (SOL), and ![][image447] (AVAX) while enforcing unitary single-leg execution whenever position notional ![][image240] and unlocking 50/50 two-tranche scaling (![][image384] and ![][image385]) only when ![][image234]3. In the third phase, the WebSocket manager subscribes to orderUpdates and userFills for the master account address2; when userFills confirms that the resting Maker Limit TP has filled, cancel\_sibling\_by\_cloid (omitting f: true) immediately purges the resting exchange-native Disaster Stop16, and if Fast-Sentinel triggers an Ioc soft-stop or giveback-ratchet exit, both the resting Maker TP and the exchange-native Disaster Stop are batch-canceled by cloid immediately upon fill confirmation8.
